title: closure
text: This is a game that only comes around every once in a while. Like Portal and Braid before it, it is a puzzle-platformer based on a simple yet complex puzzle element. Also like Portal and Braid before it, the game manages to convey a deep and meaningful story and atmosphere, all without interrupting the flow of gameplay. The puzzles are thought provoking, and make the game good on their own merit. The music, art, personality and plot make the game great. Closure is not even close to Limbo, except for the color scheme, and that a jump button exists. I only have a couple of criticisms. Being a physics-based game, the puzzles can be a bit finicky in their solution and execution. Also, the puzzles can sometimes pull focus away from the atmosphere. Spend too much time in a puzzle, and you lose focus on the larger narrative. Spend too much time in a world, and the music can get grating. This isn't so much a criticism though as high praise for the clever game design.

title: closure

Not much else in the gameplay changes dramatically, but this mechanic is probably enough to keep players interested for the duration. Having grasped object permanence in my earliest years and now having lived with it for so long, I never quite got used to it!

title: cogs
text: This is an amazing single-player puzzle game all about placing gears and pipes to transfer motion and steam from the source on one area of the grid to the goal, being a wheel, bell, or balloon, among other things. It reminds me of Pipe Dream from the classic Windows Entertainment Pack, but with beautifully updated graphics, constantly evolving 3D puzzles, and a massive Steampunk overhaul. There are three modes to play. Inventor mode is where you can take as much time and use as many moves as you need to complete the puzzle. The only goal is to complete it. Challenge mode has two variations. One is a race against the clock to finish a puzzle in 30 seconds, while the other is to finish the puzzle using 10 or fewer moves. Watch the video and get this game. It's well worth it.

title: company of heroes: tales of valor
text: What can I say about this game. I have played this game religiously since it first came out 7 years ago. The graphics remain some of the best I have ever seen. The freedom of view point allows camera angles previously reserved for cinema. It was a gaming experience like none other and few have come close to matching. The voice acting is incredible with interactive reports coming from units at all times. The AI in particular is very impressive with a progressive strategy building heavier units as the match goes on. You can actually see on the replays where the AI builds certain units to counter the units you use most. I must admit the game was better in vanilla the patches just made things complicated. I'd develop a playing style and suddenly the mg was weak or my favorite tank was now a tin can. Tales of Valor specifically added some nice gameplay and a few decent units to unlock. The campaign really made you feel for those Germans who fought for country and home rather than agenda and hatred. This game creates a bond among gamers I've never developed longterm online friendships before CoH. My one gripe and this is true for many players the US 57mm AT gun is so overpowered. It can somehow outrange anything on the map minus a hummel and destroys everything in a few hits. I understand balance is an issue because let's face it the Germans had better soldiers and weapons. In a fair fight with equal resources the allies would stand absolutely no chance. 10 million dead Russians can attest to that.
